content.text: The audit is complete; I’m only normalizing the final open/merged labels for cited PRs. No code or repository files have been changed.

I reviewed 235 unique `entireio/cli` PRs from August 10–31, 2026: 224 created during the window plus 11 older PRs closed during it. I also checked the proposed follow-ups against latest `upstream/main` at `486de6900`.

No files were changed.

## What the team is mainly working on

| Area | PRs mentioning area | Main work |
|---|---:|---|
| Checkpoints and sessions | 91 | Transcript durability, shadow checkpoints, git-refs, condensation, tokens, attach/import/resume |
| Agents and hooks | 78 | Claude, Cursor, Codex, Pi, Grok, external agents, hook reliability |
| Tests and tooling | 63 | E2E reliability, test isolation, installers, CI, logging |
| Cloud/auth/routing | 30 | Cells, jurisdictions, cluster auth, remotes, mirrors |
| Search/review/dispatch | 23 | Search UX, review execution, dispatch routing |
| Settings/configuration | 21 | Local/project settings, enable/disable, trust boundaries |
| Security/privacy/filesystem | 19 | Redaction, symlinks, filesystem confinement, credential safety |
| Explicit performance work | 15 | Batching, caching, reduced transcript parsing, fewer subprocesses |

These categories overlap. Of the 235 PRs, 87 are explicitly bug fixes, compared with 46 features and 10 explicitly labelled performance changes.

The dominant bug patterns are:

- Silent or partial checkpoint-data loss.
- Hook latency, cancellation, and subprocess lifetime.
- Wrong remote/cell/auth target selection.
- Transcript-shape drift between agent versions.
- Tests accidentally reading developer configuration or launching real tools.
- Platform-specific paths, symlinks, Windows and WSL behavior.
- Redaction and untrusted-input boundaries.
- Misleading success/error messages.

## Prioritized small bugs

### 1. Prevent merged settings from leaking across scopes

Priority: Highest  
Estimated files: 2 — `setup.go`, `setup_test.go`  
Status: Ready; no competing PR found

Merged PR [#2056](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2056) explicitly identified this follow-up. The bug remains in [current `setup.go`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/486de690083a6c69d10aa42bdeab26b3aac0d283/cmd/entire/cli/setup.go#L640-L658):

1. Adding an external agent calls `LoadEntireSettings`, producing the merged project+local view.
2. It changes `ExternalAgents`.
3. It writes that entire merged object to either `settings.json` or `settings.local.json`.

This can copy local-only paths, log settings, strategy options, or checkpoint-remote preferences into committed project settings.

Suggested title:

`fix(setup): keep external_agents writes scoped to their settings file`

Acceptance criteria:

- Only `external_agents` changes in the selected file.
- Existing fields in that file survive unchanged.
- Fields from the other settings scope are not copied.
- Tests cover local → project and project → local contamination.

This is the best high-value, reviewable bug.

---

### 2. Implement Cursor’s tool-invocation scanner

Priority: High  
Estimated files: 2 — `agent/cursor/transcript.go`, `transcript_test.go`  
Status: Ready; no competing PR found

Merged PR [#2120](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2120) confirmed that Cursor records:

```text
tool: Shell
input key: command
```

Its PR description explicitly says this resolves the blocker for `ToolInvocationScanner`. Nevertheless, current main still contains [`TestCursorAgent_MustNotImplementToolInvocationScanner`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/486de690083a6c69d10aa42bdeab26b3aac0d283/cmd/entire/cli/agent/cursor/transcript_test.go#L224-L241).

Impact: Cursor sessions remain “unsupported” for structured search-usage detection even though the checked-in real-session fixture contains everything needed.

Suggested title:

`fix(cursor): scan structured tool invocations from transcripts`

Acceptance criteria:

- `CursorAgent` implements `agent.ToolInvocationScanner`.
- `Shell.input.command` populates `ToolInvocation.Command`.
- Write/read tool calls expose their tool names.
- Hints remain a performance filter, not a semantic filter.
- Malformed lines fail open.
- The existing real Cursor fixture proves the mapping.
- Avoid copying Claude’s private walker wholesale; use Cursor’s existing transcript types to avoid duplication.

This is a good agent-integration task with concrete fixtures and no real-agent E2E requirement.

---

### 3. Make `attach` suggest the remote it actually searched

Priority: High, but very small  
Estimated files: 2 — `attach.go`, `attach_test.go`  
Status: Ready; no competing PR found

Merged PR [#1951](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1951) records a known cosmetic residual. Current [attach code](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/486de690083a6c69d10aa42bdeab26b3aac0d283/cmd/entire/cli/attach.go#L641-L649) admits that attach may search the elected checkpoint remote but print:

```text
git fetch origin ...
```

The suggested command therefore may not retrieve the missing checkpoint.

Suggested title:

`fix(attach): name the elected checkpoint remote in fetch hints`

Acceptance criteria:

- With `checkpoint_push_remote=backup`, the hint names `backup`.
- A dedicated `checkpoint_remote` still produces its resolved target.
- Election failure safely falls back to `origin`.
- Cover both v1 branch and per-checkpoint-ref hints.

This is probably the safest first contribution.

---

### 4. Return cancellation from `entire enable` instead of printing “Ready.”

Priority: High  
Estimated files: 2, if implemented at the setup boundary  
Status: Valid, but confirm the user-visible exit-code decision first

Merged PR [#1925](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1925) explicitly left this out. The import now stops on Ctrl-C, but both setup paths call the import offer and then unconditionally print `Ready.`.

A small implementation could check `ctx.Err()` after the import offer and return it before printing success.

Suggested title:

`fix(enable): preserve cancellation after history import`

Acceptance criteria:

- Interrupted import does not print `Ready.`
- The error chain preserves `context.Canceled`.
- `main.go` can produce its normal signal/exit-130 behavior.
- Ordinary best-effort import failures still allow enable to complete.
- Test both setup entry points.

Caution: open onboarding PR [#1618](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1618) also touches enable behavior, so check with maintainers before starting.

---

### 5. Bound the complete stop-hook checkpoint-finalization loop

Priority: High for pathological repositories  
Estimated files: 2 — `manual_commit_hooks.go` and its focused test file  
Status: Valid, but retry semantics need agreement

Merged PR [#2146](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2146) added per-fetch budgets but explicitly excluded the slow-but-alive network case. Current [finalization code](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/486de690083a6c69d10aa42bdeab26b3aac0d283/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go#L3168-L3188) still says nothing bounds the total loop.

Five successful 14-second fetches can still exceed a host’s 60-second hook limit even though no individual fetch times out.

Suggested title:

`fix(strategy): bound total stop-hook checkpoint finalization`

Important acceptance criteria:

- One deadline covers the whole update loop.
- Completed checkpoint IDs are removed.
- Unprocessed IDs remain for a later PostCommit/session-end retry.
- A tighter caller deadline wins.
- Codex’s `SessionEndBudgeter` is not extended.
- The test models repeated slow successes, not only a dead network.

This is more subtle than its file count suggests.

---

### 6. Remove Pi’s write-only active-session cache

Priority: Medium cleanup  
Estimated files: 3 including documentation  
Status: Ready; no competing PR found

Merged PR [#1936](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1936) says the cache became write-only after the sessionless-subagent fix. Current main still:

- Writes `pi-active-session` at session start.
- Rewrites it before each turn.
- Clears it at shutdown.
- Reads it only from tests.

Removing it eliminates pointless filesystem writes and deletes an identity mechanism already documented as unsafe for concurrent Pi sessions.

Likely files:

- `agent/pi/lifecycle.go`
- `agent/pi/lifecycle_test.go`
- `docs/architecture/agent-guide.md`

Suggested title:

`refactor(pi): remove the unused active-session cache`

## Worthwhile, but not ideal 1–2 file tasks

- Selective batch push recovery from closed PR [#1933](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1933): parse `git push --porcelain` so one diverged ref does not force every successful ref through individual recovery. Valuable performance work, but probably three files and moderately complex.
- Checkpoint metadata size guard from [#1937](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1937): valid and important, but replacing `files_touched` loses attribution unless a sidecar format exists. You already asked maintainers for a decision on this issue; wait for that decision.
- OPF index prefilter from [#2056](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2056): could reduce a 50k-file probe from roughly 23 ms to under 1 ms, but a naive byte search risks false negatives with Git index path compression. Treat it as a benchmark-and-design task, not syntactic sugar.

## Do not duplicate these

- Agent registry recursive-lock/callback problem: open PR [#1930](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1930) modifies this area.
- Claude’s obsolete 500 ms transcript wait: owned by open PR [#2099](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2099).
- Cursor UNC warning in `status`: depends on open PR [#2078](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2078).
- Final-trailer-block hardening: depends on open PR [#2168](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168).
- Rewind-reference cleanup: already open as [#2186](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2186).
- Codex `/var` versus `/private/var` test: already fixed on main.
- Git-branch checkpoint cancellation guard: already fixed on main.

## Draft PR descriptions

### Scoped settings fix

> `entire agent add` auto-enables `external_agents` by loading the merged project/local settings view and writing that merged struct into one settings file. This can copy local-only settings into committed project configuration.
>
> This change updates only the `external_agents` key in the selected raw settings file, preserving that file’s other values without importing values from the opposite scope.
>
> Tests cover both project and local targets and verify that unrelated settings remain confined to their original file.
>
> Out of scope: changing settings precedence or the behavior of other configure commands.

### Cursor scanner

> Cursor transcripts contain structured `tool_use` blocks, and current fixtures confirm that shell invocations use `Shell` with `input.command`. The previous blocker for implementing `ToolInvocationScanner` therefore no longer exists.
>
> This change implements structured Cursor tool scanning and replaces the must-not-implement test with fixture-backed scanner coverage.
>
> Out of scope: shell-command file attribution and scanning Cursor subagent transcript files.

### Attach hint

> Checkpoint reads follow the elected read-remote chain, but the recovery hint still derives its target independently and can recommend `git fetch origin` after attach actually searched another elected remote.
>
> This change derives the pasteable hint from the same lead read candidate used by checkpoint fetching.
>
> Tests cover elected remotes, dedicated checkpoint remotes, and safe origin fallback.
>
> Out of scope: changing remote election or checkpoint-fetch ordering.

The conclusions above are therefore grounded in PR descriptions, current `upstream/main`, and open-PR ownership—not claimed as transcript-backed intent.
